caption: A laptop is unplugged from its charger, and the charging light on it goes off while the screen stays on.

sa.check: A laptop with its screen on and a charger connected to it, its charging light lit.
The charger connector is pulled out of the laptop.
The screen stays on after the pull.
The charging light is on the laptop itself.
The order is lit, pull, light off with the screen still on.

pc.expect: The charging light goes out at the moment the connector leaves the port, and only then.
pc.fail: The connector is out and the charging light still shines; or the light goes out before the connector moves; or the light goes out with the connector still seated and untouched.

pc.expect: The screen's contents carry on through the pull, apart from a battery indicator changing state; windows and icons stay where they were.
pc.fail: Icons or windows vanish or appear at the moment of unplugging; or the screen's picture jumps to a different one at the pull; or a second charging light appears elsewhere on the laptop.

pc.expect: Once the connector is out the charging light stays off.
pc.fail: The charging light comes back on with the connector out; or blinks after the pull; or the connector slides back into the port by itself.

pc.expect: The cable follows the connector: it slackens and drops as the connector comes free and stays attached to it.
pc.fail: The cable stands rigid in the air; or stretches like elastic; or the connector floats beside the port.

pc.expect: One laptop and one connector on one cable; the connector leaves the port whole; the laptop keeps its shape and fingers stay outside it.
pc.fail: The connector passes out through the laptop's body rather than the port; or the connector vanishes or duplicates; or the laptop's lid or keyboard changes shape; or the cable splits.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The laptop's colour, its keyboard layout and the desk stay the same apart from the light.
pc.fail: The laptop changes colour; or the keyboard layout changes; or the port moves along the side.

note: A screen that goes dark at the pull fails S4 only: a laptop with a flat battery does go dark when unplugged, so no PC item fails for it.
